The original decay is a six-body final state: 2A → 2B + 2E + 2V. The total energy spectrum of the two E particles is continuous because the two V particles can carry away a continuous range of kinetic energy. The endpoint Q occurs when the two V particles have the minimum possible energy (their rest masses, if they are massive).

In the variant decay, 2A → 2B + 2E + M, the single massless particle M replaces the two massive V particles. The available energy increases because the rest mass of M is zero, while the two V particles had non-zero rest mass. The maximum total energy of the E particles now occurs when M carries zero energy, which is possible because M is massless. Thus, the endpoint of the E spectrum increases relative to Q. The spectrum remains continuous because M can still carry away a continuous range of energy, allowing the E sum energy to vary continuously. The shape of the spectrum adjusts due to the different phase space (one massless particle vs. two massive particles).

Answer: B
